parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: HAZOP basis: Node V-001 and associated lines (CASE-01). The design intent is not stated in the packet and is taken only as maintaining vessel integrity with an intact internal coating. Deviation: MORE corrosion/erosion (CASE-02). Recorded cause: failure at the water-system sandblasting entry, recognized as able to cause internal damage and loss of internal coating (P2). Consequence of interest: loss of internal coating in V-001 (P3); downstream integrity effects are not quantified. Safeguard: calibrated oxygen-scavenging peak (CASE-03, P1). This nominally targets dissolved-oxygen corrosion, and its coverage of the sandblasting-entry pathway is not demonstrated. Existing recommendation: monitor and calibrate the oxygen-scavenging system (P1). Likelihood: at the decision point there is no diagnostic trend, no verified initiating fault and no confirmed occurrence (P3). Coating loss is commonly a progressive degradation mode, so without any precursor the probability of the specific event within 30 operating days is judged low (~3%). It is not negligible, because the cause is credible and safeguard coverage is partial or uncertain. Predictability: the hazard class was foreseeable because it appears on the worksheet, but its occurrence and timing within the window could not be forecast from the available information (~15%). Negligence: the pre-event record shows hazard identification, a listed safeguard and a monitoring/calibration recommendation, with no ignored warning signal. No negligence is attributable, although the recommendation's implementation status is unknown. Qualitative risk: low likelihood over the stipulated horizon, with an asset-integrity consequence. No matrix category is asserted because the source rating is withheld (CASE-04) and the horizon is not calibrated to source categories. Recommendations: sustain oxygen-scavenger monitoring and calibration (P1), and verify coating condition and sandblasting-entry integrity at the next inspection opportunity. No post-event information was used.
